t: You're standing by the moat of the Tower of London, where in 2014 a sea of ceramic red poppies was laid out. The installation was called Blood Swept Lands and Seas of Red, and it marked a hundred years since the outbreak of the First World War. It held 888,246 poppies, each one standing for a British or Colonial serviceman killed in the war. The ceramic artist was Paul Cummins, and the stage designer Tom Piper shaped the overall design. It ran from July to November 2014. The title comes from the first line of a poem by an unknown soldier.
